verdict: Caution — lend selectively to small owner-run room and F&B units with verified cash flows; avoid large new capex and single-asset bets until room supply and CRZ rules are clear.
title: Port Blair tourism, hotels & restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Port Blair hotel or restaurant sells nights and meals to a visitor flow it does not control, and its cash sits in a short, seasonal cycle.** Rooms are the asset; food and beverage is the margin filler. Tourism employs nearly 75% of the population directly or indirectly [2], so the whole local economy leans on arrivals. The binding constraint is physical: of 572 islands only a few are open, land is limited, and existing hotels cannot add rooms under current CRZ rules [2]. **So when a proposal lands, check the unit's own occupancy and average room rate history, not the island's arrival story; if the borrower cannot show month-by-month occupancy, ask for the last two years of GST returns and bank statements.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the licence, the location and the room count; cash sits in the peak season and leaks in the monsoon.** November is rated a strong travel window, 23–30°C with 50–80mm rainfall and a Diwali rush [3], so the cash year starts now. Peer results show the upside is real but concentrated in branded, well-run assets: ITC Hotels posted consolidated revenue of Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, with EBITDA up 37 percent [4]; Leela's Q2 growth came from 30% RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led [6]; Ventive reported 27 per cent revenue growth with EBITDA margin at 48 per cent [5]. **These are national peers, not Port Blair comparables — use them only to see what good looks like; collect from customer the local occupancy, ARR and F&B split.**

## What has changed now
**The local trade body says the sector is in its worst growth phase, and the constraint is supply, not demand.** AATO told the Home Minister that tourist inflow has risen many-fold against available rooms, that CRZ rules block both expansion and new builds, and that e-visa at the seaport and airport is still awaited [2]. Yacht arrivals from Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia are held back by three-month visa processing [2]. Separately, the Tourism Department is leasing its own Waves Restaurant and Hornbill Guest House to ANIIDCO after spending lakhs on repairs, and past private lessees delayed vacating and damaged the buildings [1]. **That tells you state-run assets here have a poor collection and handover record, so do not lend against a government lease or a tourism-department concession without a clean, assignable agreement in hand.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue small owner-run guest houses and restaurants with a proven peak season, and asset-light operators who run someone else's property on contract.** The peer model that works is leased and managed hotels with limited capital outlay [11]. Structure term loans against the building, not against hoped-for new rooms, and keep tenor inside the CRZ approval horizon. **Take every month: GST returns, bank statements, occupancy and ARR by room type, and a season-to-season cash sweep; if receivables from OTAs or tour operators cross 45 days, ask for the ageing and hold further disbursal.** Avoid first-time developers waiting on CRZ relaxation and single-asset borrowers with no F&B or off-season income.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the booking book, not the news.** If advance bookings for the coming peak fall below the prior year, cut limits. If a borrower's OTA receivables stretch or a lease renewal is unsigned, stop fresh disbursal. If visa or e-visa policy stays unchanged through the season [2], treat foreign-arrival-dependent borrowers as weaker. Local coverage of this city's hotel finances is thin — the sources here are trade-body statements and one departmental report [1][2] — so lean on first principles and the peer benchmarks above.

Occupancy down two months running -> ask for booking book and re-rate the account
Ageing beyond 45 days -> hold disbursal until collected
Renewal unsigned or handover dispute -> treat as unsecured and stop new exposure
Bookings below prior year -> cut limit before the season starts
